candidates.research_question: Does Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) significantly reduce posttest job burnout among ICU nurses when controlling for pretest baseline burnout?
candidates.estimand: Average treatment contrast on posttest burnout adjusted for baseline burnout score
assumptions: Homogeneity of regression slopes between ACT and control groups
Linear relationship between pretest covariate and posttest outcome
Homogeneity of error variances across groups (Levene p > .05)
diagnostics: Group by pretest interaction term test for slope homogeneity
Levene test for equality of variance
Residual normality Q-Q plot and skewness/kurtosis
strengths: Controls for non-equivalent baseline differences in quasi-experimental designs
Reduces unexplained error variance, increasing statistical precision and power
Complies with Lords paradox recommendations for non-randomized pre-post groups
limitations: Requires strict homogeneity of regression slopes across conditions
Residual confounding possible if unmeasured baseline covariates exist
candidates.expected_interpretation: Significant main effect indicates ACT intervention reduces nurse burnout beyond pretest differences.

candidates.research_question: Does ACT group differ from control group on posttest burnout ignoring baseline scores?
candidates.estimand: Unadjusted posttest mean contrast between ACT and control groups
assumptions: Normal distribution of posttest scores within each group
diagnostics: Levene test for equality of variance
strengths: Does not assume linear relationship with baseline
limitations: Highly vulnerable to pre-existing non-equivalent group differences in quasi-experiments
Severely deflates statistical power by leaving baseline variance in error term
candidates.expected_interpretation: Simple mean difference between groups at posttest measurement.

candidates.research_question: Is there a significant Group by Time interaction on burnout from pretest to posttest?
candidates.estimand: Group by Time interaction effect on burnout trajectory
assumptions: Compound symmetry and sphericity of covariance matrices
Homogeneity of variance across groups at each time point
diagnostics: Boxs M test for covariance equality
Levene test at pretest and posttest
strengths: Tests both within-subject change and between-subject differences simultaneously
limitations: Does not control for baseline differences as effectively as ANCOVA in quasi-experiments
Susceptible to regression toward the mean artifact in non-randomized groups
candidates.expected_interpretation: Differential trajectory of burnout reduction across time points as a function of treatment condition.
